title: Payment service slow responses
executive_summary: INC-003 (SEV2): payment-service latency was elevated from about 18:10Z, with payment pods appearing healthy on the dashboard. The investigation status is PROBABLE_ROOT_CAUSE, not confirmed. The leading hypothesis (H1, confidence 0.63) is that a slow identity-provider JWKS refresh delays auth-service /v1/token/verify requests. This creates queueing and tail latency in auth-service, which reaches payment-service as slow verify calls and 3s upstream timeouts. Auth-service p95 rose from a 45ms baseline to a 1188ms window mean, with onset at 18:07Z (met-auth-service-p95_latency_ms-1740-1835). Auth-service p99 rose from 90ms to 1982ms (met-auth-service-p99_latency_ms-1740-1835). Payment-service timeout rate rose from 0.1 to a 2.68 window mean, with onset at 18:10Z (met-payment-service-timeout_rate-1740-1835). Auth request rate, Postgres latency, and Redis latency stayed flat, which points away from load growth and shared data-store degradation as the trigger. The critic verdict was NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE, and the investigation reached its three-round maximum. The mechanism inside auth-service remains partly unverified.

hypotheses.description: Slow identity-provider JWKS refresh (unmodelled external dependency) makes auth-service /v1/token/verify requests wait, creating queueing and tail latency that propagates to payment-service as 3s timeouts. Mechanism: Identity-provider/JWKS slowdown (first slow refresh 18:06:12Z, 480ms, after last good refresh 18:01:53Z) -> auth verify requests block on key refresh -> auth queue time rises (first 9700ms WARN 18:07:11Z) and p95/p99 step at 18:07Z -> payment-service calls to auth slow (2.3-2.7s WARNs from 18:09:13Z) -> payment p95 step at 18:09Z and 3s upstream timeouts from 18:10:19Z; api-gateway and order-service tails follow.
confidence_explanation: +0.08 proposed cause (18:06) precedes/coincides with first observed anomaly (18:07)

critic_review.summary: Auth-service is well supported as the locus of the latency: auth p95/p99 and error rate rise while request rate, Postgres and Redis stay flat, and payment's slow verify calls and timeouts follow. The specific mechanism inside auth is not yet settled. Critic re-query findings: (1) Login rate-limit WARNs are sparse and steady (7 total, roughly one every 7 minutes from 17:32:56Z), with no burst before onset. H3's cited start times (17:40:49Z / 17:50:53Z) are just sample records, and the true first occurrence is 17:32:56Z. H3 is not supported. (2) Auth CPU at 5-minute resolution is flat at about 30% through 18:05 and reaches 44% at 18:10, while p95 jumps from 46ms at 18:05 to 1981ms at 18:10. The data cannot establish whether CPU leads or lags latency, so H2's ordering is unresolved. (3) The JWKS warnings are small (480ms, declining, only 4 in the window). They cannot by themselves explain 9.7s queue waits, and the identity-provider metrics query was invalid, so H1's key link is unmeasured. No deployments were found. The only config change is payment log.level INFO->DEBUG at 17:35Z, which is a possible but unexamined contributor to payment-side overhead. Also note the 5-minute sampling makes the 18:07 onset imprecise. This is the final round, so the remaining gap should be closed with targeted queries.

assessments.reasoning: Auth-side latency onset and payment-side timeouts are consistent with auth as culprit, but the JWKS wait is small and unmeasured. Nothing shows JWKS wait accounts for multi-second queue times. Needs JWKS fetch duration per request from auth or identity-provider latency, and confirmation of which services fetch JWKS.

CPU rises about 14-16 points, with no traffic change, and error rate follows. Timing is ambiguous at 5-minute resolution: CPU onset is 18:08 to 18:10 and p95 onset is 18:07 to 18:10. Cause of CPU is unknown, and no auth config or deploy change was found. Needs a finer CPU/queue series and auth config history.

Rate-limit WARNs are sparse and steady with no burst before onset. The cited start times are sample timestamps, not first occurrences (first is 17:32:56Z). Request rate is flat, so there is no load surge. Only 7 WARNs total, too few to explain seconds of latency.

probable_root_cause.description: Slow identity-provider JWKS refresh (unmodelled external dependency) makes auth-service /v1/token/verify requests wait, creating queueing and tail latency that propagates to payment-service as 3s timeouts.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): upstream_dependency_degradation in auth-service - Slow identity-provider JWKS refresh (unmodelled external dependency) makes auth-service /v1/token/verify requests wait, creating queueing and tail latency that propagates to payment-service as 3s timeouts.
corrective_actions: Mitigate auth-service verify latency now: check the auth-service request queue and worker/connection saturation, and consider scaling out auth-service replicas or shedding non-critical verify traffic while the queue is elevated (logpat-auth-service-9246cbf2, 9700ms queue-time WARNs).

Reduce payment-service exposure to slow auth calls: review the 3s timeout and retry settings on the payment-to-auth verify path so slow auth responses do not stall payment requests (logpat-payment-service-4cb3914c, met-payment-service-timeout_rate-1740-1835).
Revert payment-service log.level from DEBUG to INFO as a low-risk step. The change was made at 17:35Z and its effect on payment-side overhead has not been assessed.
preventive_actions: Add JWKS/key-refresh caching with stale-while-revalidate behaviour, so verify requests do not block on synchronous identity-provider refresh. Set explicit timeouts and a fallback for that call (logpat-auth-service-171612d3).

Register the identity provider as a dependency in the service catalogue and metrics system. The query for 'identity-provider' failed because the service is unknown, so this gap must be closed before the next investigation.

Add per-endpoint latency and queue-time instrumentation for auth-service /v1/token/verify, separating time spent waiting on external key refresh from local processing. This would confirm or reject the H1 link directly.
Set a concurrency limit and backpressure on auth-service verify calls, so a slow dependency cannot build an unbounded queue that spreads to payment-service, api-gateway, and order-service.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert when auth-service p95 latency for /v1/token/verify exceeds 300ms for 2 consecutive minutes, and when p99 exceeds 1000ms. The 5-minute sampling used here made onset timing imprecise (about 18:07Z), so alerting should use finer resolution.

Alert on any 'Slow JWKS refresh' WARN and any 'Request queue time high' WARN from auth-service, with rate thresholds. Track both counts over time to test causal ordering (logpat-auth-service-171612d3, logpat-auth-service-9246cbf2).
Track auth-service CPU at 1-minute resolution alongside latency, so the lead/lag relationship between CPU and latency can be determined (met-auth-service-cpu_pct-1800-1820).
Alert when payment-service timeout_rate exceeds 0.5 per minute, and when payment-service calls to auth-service exceed 2000ms (logpat-payment-service-4cb3914c).
Add identity-provider health and latency metrics (p95, p99, error and timeout rates) so the external dependency is observable.
limitations: The identity-provider metrics query failed because the service is not in the metrics catalogue, so the JWKS-to-queue link (H1) is unmeasured.
Metrics were sampled at 5-minute resolution, which makes onset (about 18:07Z) and CPU-versus-latency ordering imprecise.
Logged JWKS refresh delays (480ms, declining, 11 WARNs) are small compared with the 9.7s queue waits, so they may not be the full explanation.
The auth-service CPU rise may lead or lag latency; the data cannot establish which, so H2 (CPU saturation) is unresolved.
The payment-service log-level change (INFO to DEBUG at 17:35Z) was not examined and could contribute payment-side overhead.

conclusion: The most probable explanation for INC-003 is that a slow identity-provider JWKS refresh is delaying auth-service token verification. The resulting queueing propagates to payment-service as 3s timeouts, with the signal first visible in auth-service at 18:07Z. Confidence is moderate (0.63). The status is PROBABLE_ROOT_CAUSE, not confirmed. Two gaps remain. First, the identity-provider metrics could not be queried, so the link between the external dependency and the observed queue waits is unmeasured, and the logged JWKS refresh delays (480ms, declining) are small relative to the 9.7s queue waits. Second, the auth-service CPU rise (about 30% to 44%) could not be ordered against the latency rise at 5-minute resolution, so a CPU-saturation explanation (H2, confidence 0.39) has not been excluded. The login rate-limit/load-pattern hypothesis (H3) was rejected. Mitigation should proceed now, and the evidence gaps should be closed before the root cause is treated as confirmed.
